question: Which entry is the generic local-style setter on 3.1.190, and why did the Manager's style and font calls have no effect there?
prototype_hypothesis: int32_t lv_obj_set_local_style_prop(lv_obj_t *obj, uint32_t property, lv_style_value_t value, uint32_t selector)
callsite_evidence: sub_C242E8A has the same body as the 3.1.32 setter 0xc2782ec: local style lookup for the selector, a style-property write and a style refresh.
sub_C4CF19C(obj, v) is `return sub_C242E8A(obj, 9, v, 0)`, i.e. a lv_obj_set_style_* wrapper.
The previously recorded 0xc23afe2 is `sub_C4CF19C(a1, a2); return sub_C23AF42(a1, a3, a4)` and sub_C23AF42 is two position setters, so it cannot take (obj, property, value, selector).

Mirage n67 (3.1.190, full package): with the old record every Manager label kept the default 12 px font and no card got a corner radius or a transparent background; the page-in animation also left the view at a negative x.
control_flow_evidence: Every generated lv_obj_set_style_* wrapper tail-calls 0xc242e8a with its property id.
ownership_analysis: Values are stored by value in the object's local style; a font pointer stays owned by the font manager.
unsafe_assumptions: Colours are RGB565 on this image; checked on the emulator only.
recommended_probe: Apply radius, bg_opa and text_font to a Manager row and compare the frame with the stock Settings page.
